limitations: Originality is to the best of our knowledge. The Akemann--Wright structure theorem, Pfitzner's property-(V) theorem, and the classical Bessaga--Pełczyński characterization are prior art. The claimed contribution is the compact/FSS/SS collapse for C*-algebra derivations and the c0-versus-complemented-l2 witness dichotomy. Pfitzner's 1994 article and older elementary-operator literature were not exhaustively inspected for an equivalent derivation-specific corollary.
provenance: Akemann--Wright's structure theorem for weakly compact derivations is combined with Pełczyński property (V) for C*-algebras and a rank-one fiber lemma for nonzero compact commutators. A weakly compact noncompact derivation necessarily has a nonzero component on an infinite-dimensional elementary ideal, where the commutator is bounded below on a 1-complemented Hilbert subspace.
record_title: Strictly singular derivations on C*-algebras are compact
